Rivers State Governor, Siminalayi Fubara, has described the late Albert Horsfall as a distinguished statesman. He said Horsfall’s contributions to national development brought honour and distinction to the Kalabari Kingdom and Rivers State. Fubara said Horsfall’s life of service, patriotism, integrity and commitment to humanity had left an enduring legacy that would continue to inspire generations. The governor spoke through the Secretary to the Rivers State Government, Dr Dagogo Wokoma, at the funeral service of the late elder statesman in Buguma, Asari-Toru Local Government Area of the state, on Saturday. He described Horsfall as a patriotic Nigerian whose leadership and dedication to the country’s development earned him a place in the nation’s history. Make PUNCH part of your everyday experience. No plan to shift 2027 elections — INEC chairman 2027: Groups seek probe of voters’ register discrepancies 2027: Fubara urges Rivers monarchs to remain neutral “His contributions to our nation, particularly through his service as Director-General of the State Security Service, pioneer Director-General of the National Intelligence Agency and Chairman of OMPADEC, remain significant milestones in our national history,” Fubara said. The governor noted that Horsfall’s contributions to national security, intelligence administration and the development of the Niger Delta would remain part of his enduring legacy. “His legacy of leadership, national service and dedication to development will remain an enduring source of inspiration to generations yet unborn,” he added. He urged the bereaved family, the Kalabari people and other Nigerians to uphold the values of peace, unity and selfless service exemplified by the late elder statesman. The funeral service attracted several dignitaries, including the Director-General of the Department of State Services, the Director-General of the National Intelligence Agency, a representative of the Bayelsa State Governor, the Managing Director of the Niger Delta Development Commission, the Chairman of PENDEF and the Regent of the Kalabari Kingdom. Also in attendance were the Rivers State Commissioner for Education, the Commissioner for Special Projects and other government officials, traditional rulers and stakeholders.
